wow-handler supplies admission/processing vocabulary and HandlerFuture; the sole registry and concrete thunk live in wow-world after #359. An application protocol adapter may legitimately consume that vocabulary. #584 owns making handlers thin over typed Player/Map transitions and deciding the final registry boundary from those consumers, without adding a PacketRouter trait or moving the registry merely to erase this category exception. #153 verifies the completed decision; it implements no inversion.

Directory, Group and mailbox authority have already left wow-network. The mixed wow-world application still adapts concrete session-link, framing and transport-fence contracts. This adapter consumption is not itself a second gameplay owner. #584 owns separating those legitimate protocol/lifecycle uses from any remaining gameplay-to-transport coupling, preserving socket, ordering and backpressure contracts. It may retain an evidenced adapter edge; no new trait or crate is required solely to remove the exception. #153 verifies the final classification.

Protocol handlers and presenters legitimately decode and encode wow-packet DTOs inside the mixed wow-world application crate. The debt is gameplay rules and ownership still exposed through WorldSession, not the existence of packet presentation at that edge. #584 owns complete command/query/outcome verticals that keep packet DTOs outside domain APIs and records the final adapter classification. It must not invent a crate or trait merely to make this Cargo edge disappear. #153 verifies the completed boundary.

#297 earned a transport-only kernel and #378 kept application/gameplay adapters outside it. wow-world consuming that kernel is an intended application-to-adapter relationship; wow-session retains its exact wow-network/wow-packet allowlist and may not gain gameplay, map, database or catalog dependencies. #584 owns the remaining kernel/application boundary decision after complete consumer migration. Concrete transport types need ports only if a real boundary requires them, not to erase this exception or force an application-layer reclassification. #153 verifies the decision without implementing a new abstraction.

The reputation domain still reads concrete static-data stores (reputation rank tables and progression rewards) instead of receiving them as injected DTOs. The edge exists because the catalogs are the authority for rank thresholds; retiring it belongs to the B-phase rules extraction that injects catalog views, as #584 tracks.

The reputation domain still builds its reputation-list presentation packets directly. The edge is presentation debt, not state ownership: the rank math and faction state are the domain's, and the retirement condition is moving packet construction behind the application adapter (B-phase rules extraction), as #584 tracks.

The creature CREATE projection lives in the domain crate so the map manager can hold it without depending on the wire crate; the wire crate consumes it to encode, which is the correct direction of the dependency and removes the last domain-runtime -> adapter-platform edge of the B6 map_manager extraction. The alternative is a duplicated mirror of the struct, which the structure standard forbids.
